activities.description: Narrator (Child) puts a tooth under his pillow, goes to sleep.
Narrator (Child) wakes up, finds horse manure under his pillow.
Father yells at Narrator (Child) for the horse manure.

characterInteraction.description: The father's anger towards his son, even though the son is clearly innocent, shows a lack of patience and understanding.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Sets up the comedic tone of the film by contrasting the innocence of the tooth fairy myth with the harsh reality of the Wild West.

mood.description: Starts neutral but transitions to Angry due to the father's outburst.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Mood changes from neutral to angry. The father's facial expression is clearly irritated, and his voice is loud and aggressive.

narrativeProgression.description: The child's discovery of horse manure instead of money is a humorous subversion of expectations.
The "27 years later" time jump sets the stage for the main storyline.

scenes.thematicElements: The Wild West as a dangerous and unpredictable place where even the most innocent traditions can be corrupted.

activities.description: Albert talks to Edward about the dangers of the Wild West.

characterInteraction.description: The dialogue between Albert and Edward reveals their different personalities: Albert is jaded and cynical, while Edward is naive and easily impressed.
Clinch's intimidating presence and words establish him as a clear antagonist.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Establishes the setting and introduces several key characters; emphasizes the dangers and unpredictability of the Wild West.

mood.description: Starts as Curious with Albert's narration but transitions to Anxious as the dangers of the Wild West are revealed.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Mood changes from curious to anxious with the sudden death caused by the ice block. The visuals and sound effects become more intense.
Fast cuts and rapid changes in scenery enhance the feeling of anxiety and unpredictability.

narrativeProgression.description: Albert's description of the Wild West as a "terrible place and time" sets the stage for the film's comedic take on the genre.
The ice block accident is a darkly humorous example of the absurd ways people can die in the Wild West.
Anna's introduction suggests a potential love interest for Albert.
The accidents at the fair reinforce the theme of danger and unpredictability.
Clinch's ominous announcement raises the stakes and sets up the central conflict of the film.

scenes.thematicElements: Danger, death, the harsh realities of the Wild West.

characterInteraction.description: The dialogue between Albert and Anna reveals their growing attraction to each other.
The scene with Ruth and Albert is a funny example of their mismatched personalities and perspectives on sex.
The confrontation between Clinch and Albert establishes their rivalry and the high stakes of their duel.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Shows Albert's reluctant journey towards becoming a "hero" in the Wild West.

mood.description: A mix of Excited and Anxious as Albert prepares for the duel while engaging in humorous situations.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The scene with Ruth shifts the mood towards the comical with sexually suggestive dialogue and Albert's awkward reactions.
The montage of Albert's shooting practice features funny slapstick humor, creating a lighthearted mood.

narrativeProgression.description: Anna becomes Albert's mentor, guiding him towards facing his fears.
Ruth's openness about sexuality contrasts with the conservative norms of the Wild West, adding to the film's comedic subversion.
Albert's accidental shooting highlights his lack of experience and sets up his eventual confrontation with Clinch.
Clinch's challenge to Albert creates the climax of the film's trailer.
